title: Settlement migrates in three stages from simplified accounting to real-time on-chain Base Rate accrual
content:
A.2.4.1.2.2 states the initial implementation "will occur in three stages," and the stages move along one axis: how faithfully the settlement figure is computed, and where.

Stage 1 (A.2.4.1.2.2.1.1) uses the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation with its zero floor and penalty patches. Stage 2 (A.2.4.1.2.2.2.1) drops the simplification — amounts are "calculated as specified in the Atlas without the use of the Simplified Profit And Loss Calculation" — but "interest under the Base Rate does not accrue in real time onchain and is instead calculated offchain and paid through Executive Votes," which is why it is called the Virtual Base Rate. Stage 3 (A.2.4.1.2.2.3.1) moves accrual on-chain to each Prime's Allocator Vault, after which "Executive Votes are only required to pay down accrued interest on Allocator Vaults, as necessary, and settle other amounts due."

The sequencing is well chosen because it changes one thing at a time. Stage 1 to 2 fixes the *economics* — the asymmetry disappears, and with it the need for the Distortion Penalty — while keeping the familiar off-chain, vote-driven mechanics. Stage 2 to 3 fixes the *mechanics* while leaving the now-correct economics untouched. Attempting both at once would make a failure impossible to localise.

Each stage carries an explicit tooling prerequisite (A.2.4.1.2.2.1.3.2, A.2.4.1.2.2.2.3.1, A.2.4.1.2.2.3.3.2), which identifies the real constraint: the accurate calculation is known, and what is missing is the automation to perform it monthly across every Prime. Stage 3's timing is still "to be specified in a future iteration," so the endpoint remains undated.
description: Stage 1 uses the asymmetric Simplified P&L, Stage 2 computes the Base Rate off-chain as a Virtual Base Rate paid by Executive Vote, Stage 3 accrues it on-chain in each Prime's Allocator Vault.
